rules.sentence: Depending upon the nature of movement disturbance and associated clinical features, 3 primary subtypes of catatonia are identified: akinetic (retarded) catatonia, hyperkinetic (excited) catatonia, and malignant catatonia.[27]
Retarded catatonia and excited catatonia may appear concurrently or may transition between one another in no specific order.[28]
Either subtype may progress to malignant catatonia, or the malignant form may occur in the absence of retarded or excited catatonia.[28][29]
This form is characterized by mutism, inhibited movement, posturing, negativism, and staring.[30][31]
Postures may be mundane (eg, sitting or standing in the same position for hours) or unusual (eg, head raised above the bed as if on a pillow).
Speech, spontaneous movements, and response to voice or noxious stimuli are decreased.
In more severe cases, eating and drinking may cease, and stupor and incontinence may occur.[32]
